editorial:
Imagine being a fifteen-year-old girl sent to a foreign country to marry a stranger just to keep peace between nations. That is exactly what you get with this stylish take on the life of Marie Antoinette. Instead of a boring history lesson, you get a colorful look at a lonely teenager trying to fit in at the fancy palace of Versailles. The movie feels more like a teen drama than a period piece, focusing on the parties, the shopping, and the awkwardness of her marriage to Louis XVI. You will feel her boredom and her need for attention as she surrounds herself with luxury to hide how sad she actually is.

What really pops are the costumes and the music, which make the whole experience feel fresh and modern. Kirsten Dunst does a great job showing how the queen grows from a naive girl into a woman who is out of touch with her people. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the visuals make up for it. If you love fashion and royal drama, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, but adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go if you want to see every detail of those amazing dresses.
endingExplained: As the French Revolution kicks in, the party ends and the scary reality sets in. You see the angry crowds storm the palace and the royal family get dragged away from their luxury. The movie ends with a sad, quiet tone as Marie Antoinette is taken to prison. It does not show the actual execution, but it makes it clear that her time is up. She loses everything because she ignored the poor people of France.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves fashion, royal scandals, and pretty visuals.
